correctness.rationale: Every four-part unordered partition is uniquely (a,a+u,a+u+v,a+u+v+w) with a≥1 and u,v,w≥0, and the stated e₂ expansion is verified by polynomial arithmetic. Applying weighted geometric-series derivatives gives the precise N(q)/D(q) with degN=16, degD=22 and D=(1−q)^6(1+q)^4(1+q²)^3(1+q+q²)^3. Independent exact polynomial resultant computation gives 864,32,144,36 for N against the denominator's four irreducible factors, so no factor cancels mod any p≥5. Periodicity from index zero is equivalent to (1−q^T)N/D polynomial of degree<T; coprimality gives D|1−q^T. Root orders lcm to 12 and multiplicity bound six; hence least T=12·25=300 at p=5 and 12p at primes p≥7. Independent enumeration checked 80 exact coefficients; the proof is the cyclotomic factor argument rather than finite testing.

value.rationale: A complete prime-modulus resolution of a published conjectural table is a natural exact arithmetic-combinatorial result. Proving pure least periods rather than a nonminimal period bound, including the exceptional p=5 multiplicity threshold, is genuinely informative for this weighted partition invariant.

limitations: No composite-modulus claim; no finite list of primes can certify universal minimality.
